To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) RNNs applied to a regression problem are able to model taxi drivers’ behaviour and predict the next destination; 2) RNNs trained on individual drivers’ history can generalize to other drivers, and 3) the geographical context can be exploited to further improve the results.
we propose a novel approach to predict taxi drivers’ next destination based on Recurrent Networks applied to a regression task.
we have proposed a novel approach for the taxi destination prediction, based on Recurrant Neural Networks, that is more accurate than previous approaches and that uses less information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research question: How can we use data from taxi drivers to predict the next destination?
the following questions: (i) can we predict the next taxi destination using a RNN trained on a regression problem, using as input only the starting point and the geographical features of the city?

the following questions: (i) How to use the taxi drivers’ history to predict their next destination?; (ii) How to use geographical information to improve the prediction accuracy?; (iii) How to improve taxi drivers’ destination prediction by using the starting point of the ride?; (iv) How to improve the taxi drivers’ destination by using only the starting points of the rides?; (v) How can taxi destination prediction be used to improve electronic dispatching systems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach outperforms the competition winner, and is able to provide a more robust prediction of the taxi destination, also in terms of accuracy, when compared with the baseline approach.
the proposed approach outperforms the state of the art in the taxi destination prediction, while using a limited amount of information.
the proposed approach, based on RNNs, can be considered as the state-of-the-art in the taxi destination prediction task, and it can be used as a baseline for future studies in this field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by using only the starting location of a trip, we can predict the destination of a driver with a high accuracy, thus allowing to optimize the taxi dispatching system.
we are the first to apply RNNs to the destination prediction problem, obtaining very good results in comparison to other methods.
we propose a new method that is able to predict the destination of taxi drivers based on the starting point of their rides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

RNNs, trained on the drivers’ history and using only the starting points of each ride, can be used to predict the next destination with high accuracy, thus providing a promising solution for taxi dispatching systems.
, in the context of the taxi destination prediction, the use of RNNs is more effective than the use of traditional machine learning techniques, even if they are trained on a smaller set of data.
, even if the starting point of a taxi ride is known, it is possible to predict the next destination of the driver, without any knowledge of the whole trajectory.
